name: Britto's
why_it_matters: Dominic Britto opened a five-table beach shack in 1965 that grew into a 350-cover institution. Six decades on, his prawn curry rice is the dish every first-time Goa visitor is told to order.
insider_tip: Sunset is the rush — get there before 6.30pm for a beach-view table, otherwise you're seated at the back. Open year-round, not just shack season.
signature_address: Saunta Vaddo, Baga Beach, Calangute, Bardez, Goa 403516

name: Souza Lobo
why_it_matters: Goa's oldest beachfront restaurant, started by Joao Fortunato Lobo in 1932 as a small Calangute pavilhão. Four generations later, the family still guards a Lobster Thermidor recipe they refuse to write down.
insider_tip: Skip the menu and ask for the daily catch — what arrives that morning is what's freshest. The new Bar by the Beach (added 2022) is the better sundowner spot than the main dining room.

name: Thalassa
why_it_matters: Mariketty Grana, an Athenian who married into Goa, opened a small Greek taverna on the Vagator cliff in 2003 and turned it into the state's most-photographed dining room. The flagship is now on the Siolim waterfront, run with her son Spiro.
insider_tip: Book a sunset table 7-10 days ahead in season. Belly dance Wed/Sun, LED show Thu/Sat, fire show Fri — all at 8pm. Open year-round but the Siolim river view is at its best Nov-Feb.
signature_address: Plot No. 301/1, Vaddy, Siolim, Bardez, Goa 403517

name: Bomra's
must_try: raw mango and smoked crab salad
why_it_matters: Chef Bawmra Jap, born in Myanmar, opened Bomra's in Candolim in 2003 and built a 22-year cult around modern Burmese food no one else in India was cooking. The relocated Anjuna kitchen now sits beside his own herb garden.
insider_tip: Closed Mondays in low season; open seven days Oct-May. The pickled tea leaf salad is the order — every regular asks for it. Ranked #2 at Condé Nast Traveller India's 2024 Top Restaurant Awards behind Indian Accent.
signature_address: 1152, Mazal Waddo, Opposite Our Lady of Health Chapel, Anjuna, Bardez, Goa 403509

name: Sublime
must_try: yellow fin tuna and puffed rice bhel
why_it_matters: Chef Chris Saleem moved from Bombay to Goa in 2002 and has been cooking French-technique food with Goan ingredients in restless rotation across Calangute, Anjuna, Saligao, Baga and now a Portuguese villa in Assagao — the longest-running modern fine-dining act in the state.
insider_tip: The villa courtyard seats only ~20 — book a week ahead in peak season (Dec-Jan). Lunch is calmer, lighter and the better introduction to Chris's cooking than a buzzy dinner.
signature_address: House No. 481, Bouta Waddo, Assagao, Bardez, Goa 403507

name: La Plage
signature_dish: chicken liver pâté with onion marmalade
why_it_matters: A French couple set up a wood-and-thatch shack on Ashwem Beach in 2003 and quietly defined what a Goa beach lunch should taste like. Two decades later it remains the standard everyone else copies.
insider_tip: Strictly seasonal — open mid-November to early May, closed all monsoon. Closed Wednesdays. Ask for a front-row table for the lunch sitting; the sand is two metres from your toes.
signature_address: H. No. 209, Ashwem Beach, Katte Wada Road, Mandrem, Pernem, Goa 403527

name: Tito's
why_it_matters: Tito Henry D'Souza set up a small beach restaurant on Baga in 1971 — one of Goa's first discotheques and the venue that birthed Indian club culture. The lane outside still carries his name.
insider_tip: The Courtyard restaurant opens 6pm, clubs from 9pm. Couples ₹2100, stag ₹2500, includes unlimited drinks. Skip Saturday-night queues by booking the dinner table — it doubles as your club entry.
signature_address: Tito's Lane, Baga, Calangute, Bardez, Goa 403516
